questions.question: Which of the following does NOT cause hydraulic brake failure?
questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure usually happens for two reasons: loss of hydraulic pressure or brake fade from overuse on long hills.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both side mirrors.
questions.explanation: When backing a truck, use mirrors on both sides. Get a helper whenever you can.

questions.question: To prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when you start moving, you can:

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake.
Put the vehicle in second gear.
Use the parking brake when stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake.
questions.explanation: To prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when starting after a stop, partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late to your destination, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Accept it and drive safely.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, manage your stress. If you realize you will be late, take a deep breath and accept the situation while driving safely.

questions.question: Regrooved tires:

options.text: Should not be used on any vehicle.
Should not be used on the front of a bus.
Should not be used on trucks hauling gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used on the front of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: What shows you how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.correctAnswerText: The supply pressure gauge
questions.explanation: A vehicle with air brakes has a supply pressure gauge. This gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Leave the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to drive off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle is stuck on railroad tracks, get out right away and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on signs at the crossing and call 911.

questions.question: Cargo in a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured.
Should be stacked no higher than three feet.
Should be secured so it does not move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be secured so it does not move.
questions.explanation: Cargo in a trailer must be properly secured to prevent it from shifting during transport.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Help remove water and oil from air tanks.
Are used to send air to the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help remove water and oil from air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and oil that can damage the system. Air tanks have drain valves to remove water and oil.

questions.question: When stopping, you should apply the brake pedal by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pushing down slowly and steadily.
questions.explanation: When stopping, push the brake pedal down slowly and steadily. Gradual braking helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: ____ is an example of required emergency equipment.
questions.correctAnswerText: A spare electrical fuse
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles (or six fuses or three flares), and at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while driving downhill and there is no escape ramp, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive into an open field.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail going downhill, look for an escape ramp first. If there is no ramp, find another way to stop your vehicle. This could be an open field or a side road that goes uphill or flattens out.

questions.question: When near a railroad crossing:

options.text: You should expect to hear every approaching train.
You may not hear a train, even if one is approaching.
You will hear two short blasts of a train's horn if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train, even if one is approaching.
questions.explanation: You cannot assume you will hear a train. The engineer may not blow the horn, or horns may be prohibited in that area. Noise inside your vehicle may also prevent you from hearing a train until it is very close.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Air tanks are shared between both systems.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must designate which system you are using.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: Slow down and be extra careful:
questions.correctAnswerText: When approaching a work zone.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful in work zones, where the road edge drops sharply, when objects are on the road, and on freeway ramps.

questions.question: Which of the following determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: How much you drink
questions.explanation: BAC is determined by how much alcohol you consume, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is involved in a crash down the road, you should:

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop after the crash scene and report the other driver's behavior to police.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop after the crash scene and report the other driver's behavior to police.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop at a safe distance from the crash. Wait for police and tell them what you saw.

questions.question: When starting an engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, watch your gauges. Oil pressure should reach normal within seconds.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep per day does an adult need to stay alert?
questions.correctAnswerText: Eight to nine
questions.explanation: To drive safely, you need proper rest. Most people need eight to nine hours of sleep per night to stay alert.

questions.question: When pulled off on the side of the road:

options.text: A driver should keep the driver's side door open.
A driver should turn on the emergency flashers.
The driver should wave their arms.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver should turn on the emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using the brake pedal could damage the brakes by mixing the spring force with air pressure.

questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: How fast you reach your destination.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on specific driving maneuvers and your general driving behavior. You must drive safely and responsibly. Follow all traffic signs, signals, and laws. Do not cause accidents or traffic violations.

questions.question: If you turn quickly to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do not brake because it may lock the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake because it may lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while making a quick turn to avoid a hazard. Braking could lock the wheels and cause your vehicle to skid out of control.

questions.question: What is required for pre-trip inspections?

options.text: They are needed only for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are required by law.
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require you to inspect your vehicle before every trip, no matter how long the trip is.

questions.question: When getting out of a vehicle, you must maintain ____ with the vehicle at all times.
questions.correctAnswerText: three points of contact
questions.explanation: When getting out of your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. If the vehicle is a bus, hold the handrail. Getting out incorrectly may cause you to fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: When braking a vehicle with ABS, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: With an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brake the same way you would with any other braking system. Do not brake differently.

questions.question: What may rust around wheel nuts mean?

options.text: The tires need to be replaced.

questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts could be loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check if the nuts are tight when you see rust in that area.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection with two left turn lanes, which lane should you use?

options.text: It does not matter which lane you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the right lane.
questions.explanation: You may need to swing right to make a safe left turn. Always start your left turn in the rightmost turn lane when two left turn lanes are available.

questions.question: How does an empty truck compare to a full truck when stopping?

options.text: An empty truck stops in a shorter distance.
An empty truck stops in a longer distance.
Both trucks stop in the same distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: An empty truck stops in a longer distance.
questions.explanation: Empty trucks need longer stopping distances than full trucks because they have less traction.

questions.question: When will your CDL be revoked?

options.text: When you want to add an endorsement.
When your personal driver's license is revoked.
When you have not paid a toll.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your personal driver's license is revoked.
questions.explanation: If your personal driver's license is revoked, canceled, or suspended for moving traffic violations, your CDL will also be lost. This rule does not apply if your license is revoked only for parking violations.

questions.question: What does an air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
It moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into storage tanks. A governor controls the air compressor.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning usually occur?

options.text: In areas where water collects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: In areas where water collects on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water collects on the road. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph. Under-inflated tires and worn tread make hydroplaning more likely.

questions.question: If you are disqualified from driving, what must you do?

options.text: Your employer will be notified by the state.
You must notify your employer within two business days.
You must notify your employer within a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must notify your employer within two business days.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within two business days if your license is suspended, revoked, canceled, or if you cannot drive.

questions.question: When operating a vehicle with dual air brakes, what should the driver do?

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up before driving to ensure fuel reaches the engine.
Let the air compressor build at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
Begin driving right after the vehicle starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving, allow the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. Check the air pressure gauges.

questions.question: What is blocking a load?

options.text: It is dangerous and should never be done.
It is necessary to stop cargo from moving during transport.
It is only done with liquid loads.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is necessary to stop cargo from moving during transport.
questions.explanation: Block cargo to prevent it from sliding during transport. Shifting cargo makes steering and handling difficult.

questions.question: If you have more than one driver license, what could happen?

options.text: You may get caught through the states' shared computer network.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may get caught through the states' shared computer network.
questions.explanation: All states share driver information through a computer database to stop people from getting multiple licenses. Having more than one driver license is illegal.

questions.question: Before a trip, what should you check about the pedals?

options.text: The grooved pedal surface has not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The grooved pedal surface has not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip check, make sure nothing blocks the pedals. The pedals should work properly and have grooved surfaces if they are supposed to.

questions.question: How should you warn drivers behind you that you will slow down?

options.text: Turn on the right turn signal, then the left turn signal.
Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights.
Swerve side to side to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights. This tells other drivers you plan to slow down.

questions.question: Which is acceptable during a pre-trip tire inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread of 3/32 inch in the grooves

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires made by different companies
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. All tires on the same vehicle must be the same size.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, what should the warning lights and buzzers do?

options.text: Should not light up or sound.
Should turn on and shut off quickly.
Should turn on and stay on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn on and shut off quickly.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers should turn on, then quickly turn off.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to move or warn you with their horns. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you are not sure if the road is becoming icy, what should you do?

options.text: Guess whether the road is icy.
Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: Open your window and touch the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice is on these items, the road is likely icy too.

questions.question: When should you sign a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: After each time you fuel up

questions.correctAnswerText: After defects are repaired
questions.explanation: Sign a vehicle inspection report only if defects were found and have been repaired or do not need to be repaired.

questions.question: What holds spring brakes in place while driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while driving. If air pressure drops too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: Before trying to put out an engine fire, what should you do?

options.text: Press the accelerator to use up the remaining fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as it is safe to do so. Do not open the hood when putting out an engine fire.

questions.question: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving is:

options.text: Okay if the weather is clear.
Allowed if it is for work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Against the law.
questions.explanation: Using a hand-held mobile phone while driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Compared to talking on a cell phone while driving, texting while driving is:
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on a phone. It distracts you mentally and takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: People working on a disabled vehicle on the roadside:

options.text: May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
Do not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on a disabled vehicle. They may be focused on the repair and not paying attention to traffic.

questions.question: When you apply the brakes, your vehicle should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not pull to either side.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, it means there may be a problem with the brakes.

questions.question: A speed limit posted on a ramp:

options.text: Is safe for cars, but may be too fast for large trucks.
Is just a suggestion and can be exceeded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe for cars, but may be too fast for large trucks.
questions.explanation: Speed limits on ramps are set for regular cars. Large or heavy trucks may need to go slower than the posted limit.
